reason: The cited evidence confirms that the specific HEA is a bulk, robust s-wave superconductor (E1, E2, E4), but none of the passages provide direct support for the mechanistic claims that configurational entropy causes locally varied lattice distortions, stabilizes a uniform electronic density of states, or enhances electron–phonon coupling, nor do they address the effect of reducing entropy on superconductivity.
premises: High configurational entropy in HEAs produces locally varied lattice distortions that stabilize a uniform electronic density of states.
These local distortions enhance electron–phonon coupling, driving conventional s-wave superconductivity.
Reducing configurational entropy (by removing an element) disrupts these favorable local environments and depresses or suppresses superconductivity.
The HEA (TaNb)0.67(HfZrTi)0.33 exhibits robust, bulk s-wave superconductivity at ambient pressure with Tc ~7.7 K.
